headline: IGP says police ready for ‘crossfire’ if government permits
summary: Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir faces backlash from MPs and rights groups after stating police could resort to 'crossfire' with government permission.
details: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir stated that police could resort to 'crossfire' if necessary and with government permission, sparking widespread condemnation.
The IGP made these remarks during a program in Dhaka's Chawkbazar, stating, 'Wherever crossfire is necessary, if the government allows it, we will do that.'

MP Hasnat Abdullah of the National Citizen Party (NCP) reacted sharply, warning that such remarks suggest the government is moving towards legitimising extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances.

Hasnat compared the IGP's stance to that of former controversial police officials, alleging that such conduct damages the reputation of the police force while other officers seek to regain public confidence.
The Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) and various political parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami, have also condemned the remarks as contrary to the constitution and the rule of law.
In response to the backlash, Police Headquarters clarified that the IGP did not mean extrajudicial killings by the term 'crossfire'.
Meanwhile, MP Hasnat Abdullah urged police personnel to remain neutral and not work for any political party during the upcoming elections.
Hasnat also called for the release of a female entrepreneur arrested in Mymensingh and demanded information on the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh from Mongla.
caption:
Police chief says 'crossfire' is an option if the government allows it. Backlash ensues.

Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir stated that police could resort to 'crossfire' if necessary and with government permission, sparking widespread condemnation.

The IGP made these remarks during a program in Dhaka's Chawkbazar, stating, 'Wherever crossfire is necessary, if the government allows it, we will do that.'

MP Hasnat Abdullah of the National Citizen Party (NCP) reacted sharply, warning that such remarks suggest the government is moving towards legitimising extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances.

Hasnat compared the IGP's stance to that of former controversial police officials, alleging that such conduct damages the reputation of the police force while other officers seek to regain public confidence.

The Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) and various political parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami, have also condemned the remarks as contrary to the constitution and the rule of law.

In response to the backlash, Police Headquarters clarified that the IGP did not mean extrajudicial killings by the term 'crossfire'.

Meanwhile, MP Hasnat Abdullah urged police personnel to remain neutral and not work for any political party during the upcoming elections.

Hasnat also called for the release of a female entrepreneur arrested in Mymensingh and demanded information on the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh from Mongla.

headline: 2.3 crore points: Shoriful Islam most expensive player in D3 Trophy auction
summary: The Bangladesh pacer topped the Category A players list as six franchises built their squads for the upcoming three-format tournament.
details: Bangladesh pacer Shoriful Islam became the highest-priced Category A player at the D3 Trophy Player Auction, with Citizens Bank securing him for 2.3 crore points.
Other top picks included Taskin Ahmed, who joined Walton Group for 2.1 crore points, and Tanzid Hasan Tamim, who was signed by Fortune for 2 crore points.
Fortune also strengthened its squad with Najmul Hossain Shanto (1.55 crore), Soumya Sarkar (75 lakh), and Rishad Hossain (60 lakh) points.
Further key acquisitions saw Mahedi Hasan join Blue Star for 1.6 crore, Litton Das join Walton for 1.55 crore, and Taijul Islam join Seven Rings Cement for 80 lakh.
A total of 275 players were listed for the auction, with each of the six franchises spending from a budget of 10 crore points to build a 22-player squad.
The tournament will feature 42 matches across three formats: seven four-day games, 16 one-day matches, and 19 T20 fixtures.
The T20 competition is set to begin on December 15 in Barishal, followed by the four-day and one-day tournaments in January and May next year.
The six franchises—Blue Star, Acme, Citizens Bank, Seven Rings Cement, Fortune, and Walton—will hold ownership rights for three seasons.
caption:
2.3 crore points! Shoriful Islam emerges as the most expensive player in the D3 Trophy auction.

Bangladesh pacer Shoriful Islam became the highest-priced Category A player at the D3 Trophy Player Auction, with Citizens Bank securing him for 2.3 crore points.

Other top picks included Taskin Ahmed, who joined Walton Group for 2.1 crore points, and Tanzid Hasan Tamim, who was signed by Fortune for 2 crore points.

Fortune also strengthened its squad with Najmul Hossain Shanto (1.55 crore), Soumya Sarkar (75 lakh), and Rishad Hossain (60 lakh) points.

Further key acquisitions saw Mahedi Hasan join Blue Star for 1.6 crore, Litton Das join Walton for 1.55 crore, and Taijul Islam join Seven Rings Cement for 80 lakh.

A total of 275 players were listed for the auction, with each of the six franchises spending from a budget of 10 crore points to build a 22-player squad.

The tournament will feature 42 matches across three formats: seven four-day games, 16 one-day matches, and 19 T20 fixtures.

The T20 competition is set to begin on December 15 in Barishal, followed by the four-day and one-day tournaments in January and May next year.

The six franchises—Blue Star, Acme, Citizens Bank, Seven Rings Cement, Fortune, and Walton—will hold ownership rights for three seasons.
